items.title: THIS IS ACTUAL F*CKING GOLD
items.summary:
THIS IS ACTUAL F*CKING GOLD

Anthropic just shared one of the best tricks for Claude Code.

The idea: run Sonnet, Haiku and Opus 5.5 together, each one doing only the job it's best at.

Opus-level judgment on every big call, without paying Opus rates for every routine turn.

You just launch Claude Code like this:

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

here's the split:

→ Sonnet 5.5 runs the session and writes the code
→ Haiku 5.5 explores files and docs in parallel
→ Opus 5.5 stays on call as advisor for the big calls
→ you stop spending Opus on work that doesn't need it

Opus only steps in at three moments:

→ before a plan locks
→ when the same error shows up twice
→ before calling it done

Sonnet builds. Haiku explores. Opus reviews.

JEV engineering is the same move one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) go to JEV in milliseconds, and the big models only see the ones that split

the full tree
> Sonnet 5.5 runs the main session and edits code
> search maps the repo on Haiku 5.5
> grep finds call sites on Haiku 5.5
> docs pulls the API reference on Haiku 5.5
> Opus 5.5 on call as advisor, reads the whole transcript when consulted
> JEV routes micro-forks in milliseconds

paste the tree and this prompt into Claude Code ↓

"Rebuild my Claude Code setup around this tree:
1. Run the main session on Sonnet 5.5 with Opus 5.5 as advisor.
2. Create three read-only Haiku 5.5 subagents: search (maps the repo), grep (finds call sites), docs (pulls the API reference).
3. Add one rule to CLAUDE.md: consult the advisor before locking a plan, after the same error twice, and before calling a task done.
4. Route fast deterministic forks (tool choice, path selection, retries) through JEV.
Show me every change as a diff first. No edits until I say go."

↳ https://t.co/bsYb2K5H9G

save it, you'll use this every single day.

result.actual_text:
Tôi có một số công cụ nghiên cứu để hỗ trợ tìm kiếm thông tin và dữ liệu. Dưới đây là giới thiệu về các công cụ đó:

1. **lookup**: Tìm kiếm thông tin trên web về một chủ đề cụ thể, thường được sử dụng để tìm tin tức hoặc thông tin chung.

2. **social_search**: Tìm kiếm các bài viết hoặc thảo luận trên mạng xã hội (chủ yếu là Twitter) theo từ khóa hoặc chủ đề.

3. **timeline**: Lấy các bài viết mới nhất từ một tài khoản cụ thể trên Twitter.

4. **fetch**: Đọc nội dung từ một URL cụ thể để cung cấp thông tin hoặc tóm tắt.

5. **format**: Định dạng thông tin đã thu thập thành các dạng khác nhau như tóm tắt ngắn, danh sách, hoặc theo chủ đề.

6. **deduplicate**: Loại bỏ các nguồn URL trùng lặp khỏi danh sách đã có.

7. **papers**: Tìm kiếm metadata của các bài nghiên cứu trên arXiv theo chủ đề.

8. **paper_text**: Tải và trích xuất nội dung từ một bài nghiên cứu cụ thể trên arXiv.

9. **policy**: Tìm kiếm các quy định nội bộ của công ty liên quan đến nghiên cứu, trích dẫn, bảo mật hoặc xuất bản.

Các công cụ này giúp tôi hỗ trợ bạn trong việc tìm kiếm và tổng hợp thông tin một cách hiệu quả.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: Gemini Robotics Embodied Reasoning 2 is now available on Google Cloud | Google Cloud Blog
items.summary: Earlier this year, we introduced Gemini Robotics 2 — our next-generation intelligence layer enabling robots to think, act, and adapt in the physical world. At the core of this breakthrough is Gemini Robotics Embodied Reasoning 2 (ER 2), a specialized Gemini model that serves as a robot’s high-level brain. Working across any robot embodiment — from stationary arms to full humanoids — Gemini Robotics ER 2 combines advanced spatial and temporal video understanding with long-horizon planning and [...] Gemini Robotics ER 2 transforms a robot into a physical agent. The model combines deep spatio-temporal reasoning and long-horizon planning, enabling robots to orchestrate steps to complete a task, self-correct, and generalize to novel situations. To build an agentic setup, developers can declare low-level control interfaces — like Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models or navigation APIs — as tools, and stream multimodal video, audio, or text directly into the model. [...] Today, we are bringing this same frontier embodied reasoning model to enterprise production environments: Gemini Robotics ER 2 is now available in public preview on the Gemini platform. For the first time, organizations can pair Google DeepMind’s latest embodied reasoning model for robotics with the enterprise-grade security, multi-agent orchestration, and end-to-end lifecycle management of Google Cloud — making it easier to simulate, evaluate, and deploy safe, adaptive physical AI at scale.

items.title: Synthetic-to-Real Perception for Agricultural Robotics
items.summary:
Synthetic-to-Real Perception for Agricultural Robotics

A robot working in a sugar beet field has to make a decision for every plant in front of its camera: leave it in place, or treat it as a weed. Before any tool moves, that decision depends on perception, which means locating each plant in the image and classifying it correctly. Building that capability involves two separate engineering problems. The detector must be trained on images that represent the field, and the trained model must run on embedded hardware that can be deployed, updated, and maintained on a working machine.

Konsulko Group has just posted the first of a new series of technical articles exploring Synthetic-to-Real Perception on NVIDIA Jetson platforms by Software Engineer Andjela Danilovic Nedic. 

https://t.co/vSggfQcfch
